title: Batanes voters cast ballots in special congressional election

blocks.text: BASCO, Batanes — Voting precincts opened early Saturday as residents of this province began casting their ballots in the special election to choose the province’s next representative in the Lower House.
Senior citizens and persons with disabilities, including elderly voters using wheelchairs, were among those who turned up early to exercise their right to vote.

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) is holding the special polls to fill the congressional seat left vacant following the death of Batanes Rep. Ciriaco Gato Jr. on Sept. 21. Gato was serving his third term when he passed.

Under Republic Act No. 6645, as amended by Republic Act No. 7166, a special election must be conducted to fill a permanent vacancy in the House of Representatives when it occurs at least a year before the end of the term. The law requires the election to be held within 60 to 90 days after the vacancy.

Four candidates are vying for the province’s lone congressional seat: former Batanes governor Marilou Cayco, Luis Andres Abad, retired Philippine Navy commodore Edward Ike de Sagon, and John Gato, a relative of the late lawmaker.
Comelec expects 13,138 registered voters to participate in the special polls, with voting conducted manually in 46 clustered precincts across 21 voting centers in the province.
The winning candidate will serve the remainder of Gato’s term in the House of Representatives. /dp
